title: Gorash : Where loots meet a mobile game concept
author: morganinuk2
selftext:
I'm your average developer, a jack of all trades but a master of none.

AI has allowed me to branch out to the point where almost nothing feels out of reach in the digital space.

I'm now leaning towards teaching these new tools to the people around me.

Professionally speaking, projects that used to take weeks now take hours. That has left me with plenty of time to build all sorts of apps, websites, and even games.

Recently, wanting to push things a little further, I decided to take a mobile game all the way from the initial concept to a released product.

One of my kids is fond of those playable ads game where you merge items, so I decided to merge concepts. One that he likes and one that I like. Loot-based games are kind of my thing, so there you have it : a merge/RPG roguelite.

I initially designed the game for him in september to avoid those awful ads, so obviously, no ads here. I included in apps purchases to make the game feature complete, but the economy should be generous enough not to be required.



The workflow for a month :

\- Software : Godot 4.7.2, Blender

\- VSCode w/ Claude Max x20 (Opus 5.5 / Sonnet subagents) ; GPT 6.1 Sol

\- Assets made w/ [ludo.ai](http://ludo.ai), meshy

\- SFX : Elevenlabs & Opus 5.5

\- Music : Suno

\- Skills : A few skills that I made to fluidify my workflow.

\- Browser tasks: Done by Claude browser extension following guidlines coming from Claude CLI as a markdown file. Except here, apparently ?

\- Decisions registered : 1200+ (prompts, pretty much)



Total spent is below 300 dollars. Claude Max is shared, since I usually have more than 3 runing projects at a time.

There's really nothing to brag about. I'm just sharing my experience to show that, alongside the 30-second demos we often see in this sub, there are also projects that make it all the way to a fully functional release.

It took about a month as a solo developer. I'm sure a lot more could be achieved with more time, attention, and polish, but I certainly don't intend to stop here. And I suspect neither do most of you.

Gorash is now available on Android, with hopefully more platforms to follow soon (Steam/iOS).

[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.morganvincent.gorash](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.morganvincent.gorash)

replies.author: morganinuk2
replies.body: Not really too difficult to grasp, but I guess "merge" game can be confusing for people not accustomed to mobile gaming and in-app advertisement. The idea is just to merge two similar items to get a higher level one. The fusion itself generates damage, shield, healing, summoning and what-have-you... Of course the mecanics of the game tend to stop you (items, enemies and events). At the end, you're rewarded with loot ranging from common to unique with special effects. The difficulty scales up as you progress throught the different difficulty levels.
